## Task d3ff69a5: extend color patterns into regions separated by 5-walls

Observed rule from two demonstrations and a solved test: 5-cells act as barriers/boundaries. Leave 5s and the original colored template intact; extend only into the empty region. In an L/barrier layout there may be separate regions/templates, each extended in the direction perpendicular to its seed edge.

- Demo 2: vertical 5 wall at column 0, rows 1–8; template to its right in row 7 was `4 3 3 4 4 4`, and row 8 was `7 3 7 7 3 3`. Output repeated these two rows upward, alternating, across rows 1–8, preserving the wall.

A vertical 5-barrier at column 6, rows 1–8, with bottom seed rows `[8,6,8]` and `[3,3,3]` at columns 7–9; extend these upward in alternating sequence across rows 1–8.

Practical approach: identify each straight 5-wall and any color seed placed along its open adjacent edge; determine which empty rectangular area it faces; copy/periodically repeat the seed pattern perpendicular to that edge until the next boundary or region edge. Check independent regions separately and do not overwrite 5s or seeds."
